concepts.name: The Gaussian N(0,1)
concepts.summary: The normal distribution — the bell curve. The standard normal N(0,1) has mean 0 and variance 1; draws cluster near 0. Make any Gaussian by scale-and-shift (x = mu + sigma*eps); the sum of independent Gaussians is again Gaussian, variances adding. Pure probability. (Upstairs it becomes diffusion's noise and its fixed N(0,1) endpoint.)

concepts.name: Mean and variance
concepts.summary: A Gaussian is fixed by its mean mu (center) and variance sigma-squared (spread). Standardize with z=(x-mu)/sigma; sample with x=mu+sigma*eps from a standard draw. That scale-and-shift is the skeleton of the diffusion forward step.

concepts.name: Sum of Gaussians
concepts.summary: The sum of two independent Gaussians is another Gaussian with variances added. This closure property is why a whole chain of noising steps collapses into one jump formula, and (via the Central Limit Theorem) why summed randomness is so often bell-shaped.
